exposure: High-efficacy disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in pregnant patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
outcome: Peripartum complications (hospitalizations, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, infections)
Pregnancy outcomes (completed pregnancies, terminations, full-term births)
cohort: Nineteen patients with a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) who became pregnant and were seen in the Duke MS clinic, encompassing 34 pregnancies.
finding: The majority of deliveries in this contemporary cohort of pregnant patients with MS on high-efficacy DMTs resulted in full-term births.
mod_finding: The most common form of delivery was cesarean section (69% of deliveries).
